# Compiler IR v1

<!-- Generated by scripts/check_spec.py from docs/spec/compiler-ir.toml. Edit that file and run `python3 scripts/check_spec.py --write`. -->

This specification records the planned compiler path from the exact accepted Lean Core through the optimization and execution phases of one Vastitas MidIR to the exact bytes of an LLVM module. The current compiler emits Lean and has its own checked path. All claims on this page are Planned. First measure official-kernel and Fast replay on a representative MidIR artifact of about 1,000 operations, and qualify the LLVM toolchain, linked Lean runtime and numerical adapter on Linux and macOS. Then deliver the constructor coverage and opcode registry, the modeled LLVM subset and exact emitter, the validators and composition proofs, and the native handoff and evidence.

[Specifications](../specifications.md) defines the [claim statuses](../specifications.md#claim-statuses) and the checks. This chapter is generated from [`docs/spec/compiler-ir.toml`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/docs/spec/compiler-ir.toml).

<a id="compiler-ir.source.acceptance"></a>

## Both modes start with the same accepted Core

- Property: `compiler-ir.source.acceptance`
- Subject: `Finite source admission`
- Rule: [Planned LLVM compiler path](../development/architecture.md#planned-llvm-compiler-path)

The edition-2026 manifest and finite grammar use schema epoch 10 for packages and normalized single-file inputs. The Lean checker independently accepts the actual input, including the selected finite function or method, package and assembly revisions, and retains the exact Core and its checks. Both modes use that same result. The Rust frontend and any serialized IR supply candidates. The source, module and evidence stay tied to the same dependency and Charter environment. The finite source, category, tensor and exact RR/CC cases enter the release matrix with their actual acceptance and rejection evidence.

- Example: A flat file and a package each use the sole current wire schema. A forged method winner cannot grant acceptance.
- Not executed: The finite edition-2026 source profile and its complete source-to-Core evidence are pending.

Claims:

- `source`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#762](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/762)

<a id="compiler-ir.midir.phases"></a>

## A single typed IR has two phases

- Property: `compiler-ir.midir.phases`
- Subject: `Phase-indexed MidIR modules`
- Rule: [Planned LLVM compiler path](../development/architecture.md#planned-llvm-compiler-path)

A v1 module records its phase, admission profile, source and dependency revisions, target triple, data layout, ABI and numerical policy. The Lean representation has functions, typed SSA block parameters, operations and terminators. It retains selected body, method and assembly identities, nominal types and endpoints, and explicit control and effect ordering. Verify CFG targets, argument types, dominance and symbol resolution on actual artifacts. Optimization retains the source-selected algorithm and the mathematical facts needed for rewrites. Execution makes guards, layouts, cleanup and ABI choices explicit. Typed dumps round-trip as bounded untrusted candidates. The ownership authority is the kernel storage checker over the accepted plan. MidIR validators preserve initialization, aliases, permissions and ownership by refinement. Witnesses for allocation, alias or release changes relate both plans. Proof-only data may be erased after the checks that use it.

- Example: A join checks its block arguments and preserves the move and initialization obligations of both branches.
- Not executed: The phase-indexed constructors and their validator are pending.

Claims:

- `representation`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#750](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/750)

<a id="compiler-ir.midir.registry"></a>

## The operator registry is closed

- Property: `compiler-ir.midir.registry`
- Subject: `Admitted MidIR operations`
- Rule: [Planned LLVM compiler path](../development/architecture.md#planned-llvm-compiler-path)

The registry assigns each admitted Core and storage operation a phase, typing rule, denotation, lowering obligation and explicit result or effect contract. Publish constructor coverage against a named accepted-Core revision and regenerate it when the admitted constructors change. Unsupported operators fail admission. Tensor operations retain mathematical axes, bases, tensor versus map identity, dual and conjugation roles, and the separate storage layout. Rewrites of an admitted reverse-AD operation preserve both its primal and selected pullback. Equal dimensions do not select an identity or a method.

- Example: A contraction with equal-sized axes still rejects a mismatched nominal endpoint.
- Not executed: The closed MidIR registry and its source coverage ledger are pending.

Claims:

- `registry`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#751](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/751)

<a id="compiler-ir.native.contract"></a>

## Numerical execution uses declared foreign calls

- Property: `compiler-ir.native.contract`
- Subject: `The NativeFast and Lean runtime premises`
- Rule: [Planned LLVM compiler path](../development/architecture.md#planned-llvm-compiler-path)

Indexed primitives and arbitrary-precision Nat and Int call one Lean-compiled runtime library under a labeled foreign premise. A C shim exposes operations that the runtime offers only inline. Each admitted Nat or Int operation is a call in this profile. Represented floating values stay in the resource layer and cross LLVM as bits and arguments to adapter calls. All four F32/RR, F64/RR, F32/CC and F64/CC representations are required. GEMM uses the pinned sequential LP64 OpenBLAS 0.3.34 adapter for sgemm, dgemm, cgemm and zgemm under a labeled host/build-specific premise, with the corresponding real or interleaved complex layout. A program that needs no numerical runtime requires no OpenBLAS. Fixed-order adapter results follow the reference result bits, with a NaN class where the reference does not specify the sign or payload. OpenBLAS results have the stated determinism premise on one pinned build and host. Error bounds and numerical correctness claims need their own evidence. The NativeFast flags observation is unavailable. Its storage expectation uses IEEE equality and a NaN expectation tests for NaN. Preserve foreign-call identity, argument bits and order even where an observation abstracts the result. The modeled LLVM subset emits no floating-point instructions and rejects strict, LLVM-default and unadmitted sign-observing profiles. Admitted division is totalized. The ordered same-precision scaled complex quotient uses totalized real divisions and fixes the order and effects of the graph, with inverse through the same graph. Emit no fallback, FMA or raw CUDA division substitution. Float values gain no public pure-Core float carrier. SafeFloat and the Result forms of safe division wait for the Result language support.

- Example: A complex GEMM lowers to the selected adapter symbol with the original layouts and arguments, while the receipt records flags as unavailable.
- Not executed: The required four native realization rows for the verified LLVM path are pending.

Claims:

- `operations`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#751](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/751)
- `realization`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#753](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/753)

<a id="compiler-ir.validation.refinement"></a>

## Each validated stage preserves the selected observations

- Property: `compiler-ir.validation.refinement`
- Subject: `Independent Lean validation`
- Rule: [Planned LLVM compiler path](../development/architecture.md#planned-llvm-compiler-path)

Define observation semantics and refinement in a dedicated namespace of the mathlib-free VastitasOracle. Its denotation uses kernel artifact types and is independent of the implementation of the validators. A stage checks a bounded, untrusted witness against the actual input and output. Prove soundness for every witness. Compose per-function checks with an independent module, symbol, call, ABI, effect and ownership check. Validate selected numerical graphs, ordering, relevant bit identity, runtime and resource premises, and the actual exact emission. A local witness that changes a caller's ABI or a wrong order of contravariant composition fails the composed check. Stage validation joins the applicable finite CS, MS and CF obligations for the same accepted source, environment, Core and evidence. It grants no other checker or proof-export path source acceptance authority.

- Example: Two locally valid functions with mismatched calling conventions fail the whole-module check.
- Not executed: Actual-artifact validation and the finite constitutional proofs are pending.

Claims:

- `validation`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#752](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/752)
- `constitution`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#763](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/763)

<a id="compiler-ir.validation.modes"></a>

## Proof evidence binds the current build

- Property: `compiler-ir.validation.modes`
- Subject: `Fast and Official verification`
- Rule: [Planned LLVM compiler path](../development/architecture.md#planned-llvm-compiler-path)

Fast is the default and audits a Lean proof export using the matching toolchain's pinned out-of-process nanoda_bin. Official uses current-run pinned official Lean kernel replay and reduction. Both authenticate the exact source, dependency and Charter environment, Core, mid-level artifacts, complete LLVM bytes and allowed axiom closure. Unsupported export forms, stale evidence, native-evaluation shortcuts and failed internal obligations must fail closed. Constitutional CI uses only the official kernel for the language-wide claims. A successful standalone proof-export diagnostic alone does not grant a build result. Artifact caching may not waive evidence. Record mode, verifier and whether the official kernel checked the current build. Diagnostic reports and inspection commands project actual pass events, rather than supplying accepted witness data. Format errors in those reports remain diagnostic. Keep source acceptance, exact emission, external premises, native evidence and performance results visible independently.

- Example: A proof for the same function name and different LLVM bytes fails in both modes.
- Not executed: Current-artifact mode integration is pending.

Claims:

- `verification`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#752](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/752)

<a id="compiler-ir.llvm.bytes"></a>

## Validation covers the bytes supplied to LLVM

- Property: `compiler-ir.llvm.bytes`
- Subject: `Modeled LLVM emission and native handoff`
- Rule: [Planned LLVM compiler path](../development/architecture.md#planned-llvm-compiler-path)

Use an independently modeled finite LLVM subset and check the actual deterministic text by bounded parsing and exact artifact correspondence. Compare the final file with the validated complete bytes before passing those bytes to the untrusted parser. Disable unproved overflow, alias and inbounds promises and unsupported instruction forms. Fail a changed byte, ABI, target, layout or missing proof before invoking LLVM. The isolated Cargo-linked adapter uses llvm-sys 231.0.1 and qualifies LLVM 23.1.4 as the first exact native candidate on Linux and macOS. Pin the native library and link mode, runtime and adapter, pass and target-machine options, linker, triple and layout. Prefer static libLLVM linkage for supported prebuilt releases. LLVM's parser, optimizer, object emission and linker remain external premises. A Lean/C build is a separate compiler path. Record native coverage and equivalent-C timings, allocation, copies and peak memory independently of the exact-emission proof.

- Example: Changing one byte of the verified .ll file causes the final handoff to reject it.
- Not executed: The modeled emission, byte check and native handoff remain pending.

Claims:

- `emission`: [Planned](../specifications.md#planned)
  - Issue: [#753](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/issues/753)
